correctness.rationale: Set U=u+1, A=2Uv, B=U²−2nv² and C=U²+2nv²; expand C²−B²=8nU²v²=2nA². For c!=0, x=−cnA²,y=−cB²,z=C² gives F_c(x,y,z)=c²n²A⁴ and t=c²n²A³BC squares nxyzF. For c=0, x=nA²,y=B²,z=C²,t=nABC(nA²+B²) likewise solves. In Q[u,v], A and B are coprime because B has nonzero U² coefficient and nonzero v² term for n≠0, so x and y share no nonconstant factor. Since z=C² has u⁴ coefficient 1, no common integer prime content exists. Symbolic independent polynomial checks validate both branches for arbitrary formal n,c, beyond finite parameter substitution.

For n!=0, c in Z, direct symbolic identity C²−B²=2nA² makes t²=nxyzF_c exactly in both c=0 and c!=0 branches; z=C² has coefficient 1 of u⁴, so no integer common content.

originality.rationale: Gawron–Ulas 2015 already prove polynomial-coprimality at n=1 (Corollary 2.2) and nonexceptional forms for general n, and primitive integer solutions for exceptional forms. Their Remark 2.3 and Conjecture 2.4 explicitly separate the unsettled integer-polynomial-coprimality case when n is arbitrary in the exceptional family. Thus the n=1 subcase and integer solutions are prior; the new uniform explicit exceptional polynomial family for every n!=0 is the assessed remainder. Searches found no stronger covered solution; unindexed preexisting parametrizations remain a risk.
residual_risks: The n=1 instance is already proved in the cited paper; novelty is the all-n exceptional family, not the n=1 case.
A subsequent unlocated answer to Conjecture 2.4(a) might supply the same construction or a theorem subsuming it.
